purpose: Declared, authorized divergences between a sealed attempt's product-file attestation and the live working tree. A sealed RAH attempt records the hashes of the product files it wrote; that record is history and stays immutable. When a later authorized change edits one of those files, the sealed hash stops reproducing. That divergence is legitimate, but it must never be silent, so every instance is declared here and checked by tests/packaging/test_sealed_pin_integrity.py.
contract: An entry exempts exactly one (path, sealed_by, sealed_hash -> superseding_hash) transition. It is not a permanent exemption for the path: if the file changes again, superseding_hash stops matching disk and the gate fires.
An entry whose sealed_hash already matches disk is a dead exemption and is itself a failure, so the registry cannot accumulate cover for drift that has not happened.
Deleting a pinned product file is never a supersession. A missing pinned file is always a failure.
Entries are append-only in spirit: correct a wrong entry by superseding it, do not rewrite history to make a gate pass.

authorized_by must name a decision_id resolvable at artifacts/authority_decisions/<id>.human-decision.json whose affected_artifact_ids cover the path. A free-text justification is not an authorization: an earlier version of this file cited a SPEC_GAP id that existed nowhere but this file, which is a circular record, and another entry cited the author authorizing its own work.

supersessions.reason_text: Regenerated by scripts/build/canonical_registry/materialize.py after two authorized amendments to schemas/: the source_locator nullable-page change that closed SPEC_GAP-SOURCE-LOCATOR-PAGE, and the document-registration field_sources mapping that made its canonical-hash preimage resolvable from the schema alone. The canonical projection is a build output of schemas/, so amending the authoring source necessarily moves this file; leaving it stale would make the runtime read a contract the repository no longer declares. The second amendment was caught by this very gate: the first supersession entry stopped matching, which is the intended behaviour rather than a standing waiver.

Bundle-hash pins re-anchored to the amended schema set, twice. Every prior pin value is retained in comments in the file so the moves stay auditable rather than erased, and the test still fails closed if the bundle changes again without a deliberate re-pin.

Two assertions pinned claims about the world rather than invariants: 'specified_only == []' and 'a specified-only component has no package directory'. Together they forced the maturity report to overclaim, which is how retrieval, providers and shinka_adapter came to be reported as implemented while none could execute. Both were replaced by a classification invariant: no shipped package may escape the report in either direction. An earlier version of this entry called that replacement 'strictly stronger', which is false — the old and new assertions are near-negations and therefore incomparable — and the overstatement is corrected here rather than left standing. This is still the one class of edit a sealed test hash must not be allowed to freeze, because freezing it would make the seal enforce the overclaim.

Projection of the authoring schema after x-canonical-identity gained an explicit exclusion_policy. An independent review found that the identity block enumerated 6 preimage fields, declared no excluded_fields, and therefore left 34 properties unclassified while the new contract gate skipped it entirely — the gate passed vacuously on the one live block it should have caught. The policy states that identity is exactly the listed fields and stays closed to later additions, which is the required semantics for an identity digest: silently widening it would change the identity of records that did not change and invalidate every candidate id already issued. No digest value changed.

Regenerated by its declared generator after the canonical schema amendments. Before this, the file was sealed-pinned and byte-unchanged, so the pin gate passed it while it embedded the pre-amendment source digest sha256:19e12fe0affb -- the dependent-projection failure class, surviving one layer outside the gate that was built to close it. The generator's own --check reported it stale; it now reports zero stale files.
